Other times, we might notice that a routine has become a kind of safe harbor, but no longer feels alive or purposeful.

One way to distinguish between genuine renewal and clinging to old comforts is to notice how these routines make you feel over time. Do they leave you feeling refreshed, inspired, or quietly content? Or do you sense a kind of dullness, or a longing for something different? You might also ask yourself: Are these routines helping me grow, or simply helping me feel safe?

It can help to gently experiment—perhaps by introducing a small change to a familiar routine, or by trying something new alongside it. Notice how you respond. Sometimes, even a subtle shift can reveal whether you’re ready for renewal, or whether the comfort of the familiar is what you need right now.

Above all, be kind to yourself as you explore these questions. There’s no “right” answer—sometimes comfort is exactly what we need, and sometimes renewal comes quietly, in its own time. Your willingness to reflect and listen to yourself is already a meaningful step. Keep exploring, and trust that your own sense of what feels true and nourishing will guide you.
